# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm docs:gen` from the command registry (`engine/tools/registry.ts`, `defaultRegistry()` in `engine/tools/main.ts`). Do not edit by hand: `pnpm docs:check` (part of `pnpm test`) fails when this page is out of date. -->

Every block below is exactly what `pnpm cli help` and `pnpm cli help <command>` print. Add `--json` to any
command for one JSON result object on stdout. The rules behind each command are in
[engine/tools/CLAUDE.md](../../engine/tools/CLAUDE.md); file formats are in [schemas.md](schemas.md).

## Overview

```text
Usage: pnpm cli <command> [arguments] [flags]

Commands:
  help        list the commands, or show one command with its arguments and flags
  validate    check every content file of a game against its schema (starts nothing)
  run         play a run file headless from its seed and check its assertions and invariants
  dump        the whole game or world state at one tick of a run file, as JSON
  trace       a few snapshot paths over a range of ticks of a run file, one row per traced tick
  code        the save code of a game run's campaign save at its last tick (or --tick N)
  screenshot  a PNG of one paused, seeded frame of a run file (headless Chromium)
  mutants     play run files once per kit rule switched off and report the rules they don't guard
  get         read one value of a content file (path dotted or a JSON pointer); text-map rows with a ruler
  set         replace one value of a content file; checked, written, read back and verified
  add         append to an array, insert at an index (- is the end) or add a new key; verified like set
  remove      delete a key or an array item of a content file; verified like set
  paste       write a block of lines over a text map from one cell; verified like set

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file

Exit codes:
  0  ok              the command did what it was asked and every check passed
  2  usage           bad command line: unknown command or flag, a missing or extra argument
  3  invalidContent  a content file (or game.json) breaks its schema; the result names the file and field
  4  failedCheck     the content is valid but a check failed (a run's assertion, screenshot's WebGL renderer check)
  5  crash           an exception: a bug in the tools, the engine or the game

Run "pnpm cli help <command>" for one command.
Reference pages: docs/reference/cli.md (commands) and docs/reference/schemas.md (file formats).
```

## `help`

```text
pnpm cli help [command]

  list the commands, or show one command with its arguments and flags

Arguments:
  [command]  the command to show; all of them when left out

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `validate`

```text
pnpm cli validate <game>

  check every content file of a game against its schema (starts nothing)

Arguments:
  <game>  the game folder, such as games/demo

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `run`

```text
pnpm cli run <runFile> [flags]

  play a run file headless from its seed and check its assertions and invariants

Arguments:
  <runFile>  the run file, such as games/demo/runs/walk-east.run.json

Flags:
  --disable-rule <string>  kit rules to switch off, comma-separated ids (see `mutants`), on top of the run file's

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `dump`

```text
pnpm cli dump <runFile> [flags]

  the whole game or world state at one tick of a run file, as JSON

Arguments:
  <runFile>  the run file, such as games/demo/runs/walk-east.run.json

Flags:
  --tick <number>  the tick to show (0 is the start, before any step)

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `trace`

```text
pnpm cli trace <runFile> [flags]

  a few snapshot paths over a range of ticks of a run file, one row per traced tick

Arguments:
  <runFile>  the run file, such as games/demo/runs/walk-east.run.json

Flags:
  --paths <string>  the snapshot paths to read, comma-separated dotted paths (hero.x,hero.room)
  --from <number>   the first tick to trace (default 0, the start)
  --to <number>     the last tick to trace (default the run's ticks)
  --every <number>  trace every K-th tick from --from (default 1)

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `code`

```text
pnpm cli code <runFile> [flags]

  the save code of a game run's campaign save at its last tick (or --tick N)

Arguments:
  <runFile>  a game run file, such as games/samples/mini-siege/runs/played.run.json

Flags:
  --tick <number>  the tick to take the code at; the run's last tick when left out

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `screenshot`

```text
pnpm cli screenshot <runFile> [flags]

  a PNG of one paused, seeded frame of a run file (headless Chromium)

Arguments:
  <runFile>  the run file, such as games/demo/runs/walk-east.run.json

Flags:
  --tick <number>             the tick to draw (0 is the start, before any step)
  --out <string>              where to write the PNG (default .ww-out/screenshots/<run name>-t<tick>.png)
  --backend <canvas2d|three>  what draws it: canvas2d (the view's render) or three (its frame() and the game's three skin)
  --allow-software-gl         three only: take the picture on software WebGL (SwiftShader) instead of refusing (exit 4)

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `mutants`

```text
pnpm cli mutants <target>

  play run files once per kit rule switched off and report the rules they don't guard

Arguments:
  <target>  a run file (games/demo/runs/walk-east.run.json), or a game folder (games/demo) for every run file of the game

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `get`

```text
pnpm cli get <file> <path> [flags]

  read one value of a content file (path dotted or a JSON pointer); text-map rows with a ruler

Arguments:
  <file>  the file: game.json, a content file, a text-grid part (.map.txt) or a run file
  <path>  where in the file: dotted (frames.idle.2, legend["#"]) or a JSON pointer (/frames/idle/2); "" or . is the whole file; in a text grid also rows.R1-R2 (rows R1 to R2) and rows.R1.C1:R2.C2 (a rectangle, corners included)

Flags:
  --ruler  text grids: show the rows (rows, rows.R1-R2 or a rectangle) under a column ruler, each with its row number

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `set`

```text
pnpm cli set <file> <path> <value>

  replace one value of a content file; checked, written, read back and verified

Arguments:
  <file>   the file: game.json, a content file, a text-grid part (.map.txt) or a run file
  <path>   where in the file: dotted (frames.idle.2, legend["#"]) or a JSON pointer (/frames/idle/2); "" or . is the whole file
  <value>  the value, as JSON ("5", "[1, 2]", "{\"a\": 1}"); text that is not JSON is taken as a string

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```

## `paste`

```text
pnpm cli paste <file> <at> [block] [flags]

  write a block of lines over a text map from one cell; verified like set

Arguments:
  <file>   the text-grid part file (.map.txt)
  <at>     the block's top-left cell, rows.R.C (row R, column C)
  [block]  the block: lines of equal width split by \n (typed as two characters) or line breaks, or @path for a file holding them (\@ for a block starting with a real @)

Flags:
  --from-file <string>    read the block from this file instead of the <block> argument
  --transparent <string>  a block character that leaves the cell under it as it is (default: none, every cell is written)

Global flags:
  --json                 print exactly one JSON result object on stdout
  --help                 show help for the command
  --max-output <number>  the output cap in bytes; longer output is cut and the rest written to a file
```
